chunk_findings.detail: `own_distribution()` only searches `_paths.package_parent()`, i.e. the directory that contains the `ddflow` package. For a PEP 660 editable install (`pip install -e .`, `uv pip install -e .`) that directory is the project root, but the PEP 610 record is not there: pip/uv write `direct_url.json` (with `dir_info.editable = true`) into the `ddflow_mcp-*.dist-info` in `site-packages`. So `install_info().kind` can never be `"editable"` for a real editable install. With hatchling/uv (no metadata directory left in the tree) `own_distribution()` returns `None` and `_kind` falls into the `dist is None` branch, yielding `"source-tree"`; with setuptools, `pip install -e .` leaves a `ddflow_mcp.egg-info/` directory in the project root, which `importlib.metadata.distributions(path=[root])` does find, and since that egg-info has no `direct_url.json` (pip writes it into the installed dist-info, not the build artifact) `_kind` returns `"index"` for a dev checkout. That last case is not just a wrong label: `installed_from_index()` then also returns `True`, i.e. the helper asserts that `uvx ddflow-mcp` reaches the same project, which is exactly false for an editable dev tree — the opposite of the intent ("`editable`" is one of the advertised kinds, and a fixture with `dir_info.editable` is supposed to be detected).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:install_info (via own_distribution / _kind)

chunk_findings.detail: `text.replace(home, "~")` has no path-component boundary check, so it corrupts any path whose first component merely starts with the same string as the home directory. Given `HOME=/home/ann` and a package living in `/home/anna/checkout/ddflow`, `normalise_path("/home/anna/checkout")` returns `"~a/checkout"`, not `"  /home/anna/checkout"` with the home replaced — the returned location is a mangled path (and for a home like `/home/a` with a tree under `/home/ab/...` it produces `~b/...`). A check such as `text == home or text.startswith(home + os.sep)` avoids this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:normalise_path

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `E._running_from_source() == I.running_from_source() == A._running_from_source()`, i.e. it compares the *return values* of the three functions, not their identities. In any environment this is just `bool == bool == bool`, which is true whether `adopt`/`enforce` actually alias the factored implementation or each keep their own private third copy that happens to return the same boolean. Since the whole point of the change ("reuse … rather than a third copy: factor it") is to eliminate duplicate implementations, this test gives zero protection for the invariant it is named after: I can revert the factoring, leave `A._running_from_source`/`E._running_from_source` as independent copies, and this test still passes. A check of `A._running_from_source is I.running_from_source` (or `__module__`) would be needed to detect the regression.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_install_info.py::test_adopt_and_enforce_share_the_one_implementation

chunk_findings.detail: The test creates a throwaway repo and runs a real `git commit` with `subprocess.run(..., check=True)`, but only overrides `user.name`/`user.email` via `-c`; it does not disable signing. On any machine whose global `~/.gitconfig` sets `commit.gpgsign = true` (a common developer setup), `git commit` fails with "gpg failed to sign the data", `check=True` raises `CalledProcessError`, and the test errors out even though `install_info` is perfectly correct. Passing `-c commit.gpgsign=false` (and `-c tag.gpgSign=false`) would make the fixture independent of the ambient git configuration.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_install_info.py::test_source_tree_reads_the_commit_from_git (the `git(...)` helper call `commit -q --allow-empty -m x`)

chunk_findings.detail: `installed_from_index()` decides purely on `own_distribution()` + absence of `direct_url.json`, and never consults `running_from_source()`. The comment added in `install_info()` states the opposite rule ("A checkout is never an index install, even when a build leaves an egg-info (no direct_url.json) beside it"), but that guard is only applied to `kind`, not here. Concretely: `own_distribution()` looks beside the package via `_paths.package_parent()`, and this repo is flat-layout (`is_own_dev_tree` checks `(root/"ddflow").is_dir()` and `pyproject.toml` at that same `root`), so a legacy editable build that leaves `ddflow_mcp.egg-info/` at the repo root makes `metadata.distributions(name=..., path=[repo_root])` return a distribution whose `direct_url.json` is absent. `installed_from_index()` then returns `True` while `install_info().kind == "source-tree"` for the same process. Callers that use this to choose the index (`uvx ddflow-mcp`) path would pick it for a checkout.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py `installed_from_index`

chunk_findings.detail: The `root` argument does not influence the two things that decide `kind`: `from_source = running_from_source()` is computed from `Path(__file__)` and `dist = own_distribution()` from `_paths.package_parent()`, both of which always describe the *running* process, not `root`. The docstring promises "`root` is the directory holding the `ddflow` package". Demonstrated failure: when the code is being run from the repo checkout (as any fixture-based test of this helper will be), `from_source` is `True`; calling `install_info(root=<fixture tree with a `vcs_info`/`dir_info` direct_url.json>)` then executes `record = _editable_record(root)`, which finds nothing (the record is not editable / not in site-packages), so `_kind(dist, None, True)` returns `"source-tree"` instead of `"vcs"`/`"local-dir"`/`"index"`. The documented per-kind behaviour of the public `root` argument is therefore unreachable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py `install_info` / `running_from_source`

chunk_findings.detail: The `file://` URL is used verbatim: `Path(url[7:]).resolve() == root.resolve()`. PEP 610 requires these URLs to be percent-encoded (RFC 8089), and pip/uv write them via `pathname2url`, so an editable install under a home directory containing a space or non-ASCII character yields a URL like `file:///home/ann/My%20Project`. `Path("/home/ann/My%20Project").resolve()` never equals `Path("/home/ann/My Project").resolve()`, so the record is skipped, `record` becomes `None`, and `kind` is reported as `"source-tree"` instead of `"editable"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py `_editable_record`

chunk_findings.detail: The first assertion is `assert E.running_from_source is I.running_from_source`, i.e. it reads a *public* attribute `running_from_source` off `ddflow.services.enforce`. But the change description says the existing implementation lives in `enforce._running_from_source` (private), and the very next line of the same test uses that private name (`E._running_from_source() == I.running_from_source() == A._running_from_source()`). The public name is the one the new `install_info` module re-exports, so under the described factoring `install_info.running_from_source` *is* `enforce._running_from_source`; enforce itself has no `running_from_source`, and the assertion raises `AttributeError: module 'ddflow.services.enforce' has no attribute 'running_from_source'`, erroring the test instead of verifying the shared implementation. The `is`-vs-`==` pattern confirms this: enforce/install_info are meant to be the *same object* (hence `is`), while adopt is only value-equal (hence `==`). The line should be `assert E._running_from_source is I.running_from_source`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_install_info.py::test_adopt_and_enforce_share_the_one_implementation

chunk_findings.detail: `_editable_record` compares `Path(url[7:]).resolve() == root.resolve()`, but the PEP 610 `url` is a real URL and therefore percent-encoded, while `Path(url[7:])` performs no decoding. For an editable install whose project lives in a path containing a space (or `#`, `?`, non-ASCII, etc.), the record's `url` is e.g. `"file:///home/ann/my%20project"`, so `Path("/home/ann/my%20project").resolve()` is `/home/ann/my%20project`, which never equals `root.resolve()` = `/home/ann/my project`. `_editable_record` then returns `None`, and because `running_from_source()` is `True` for an editable install, `install_info` falls through to `_kind(dist=None, record=None, from_source=True)` and reports `kind == "source-tree"` instead of `"editable"`. Concretely: put a clone in `/home/ann/my project`, `pip install -e .`, then `install_info().kind` returns `"source-tree"`, which is wrong — it is an editable install. The URL path needs `urllib.parse.unquote` (or `urlparse`/`pathname2url` round-trip) before comparison.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py: `_editable_record`

chunk_findings.detail: The module docstring promises "Nothing returned names a home directory, and a URL is never returned at all: it can carry credentials", and the stated intent is "no private path in the output (home dirs are normalised)". But `direct_url` is a public, exported function (`__all__`) that returns the raw PEP 610 record, including the `url`. Given a VCS install whose `direct_url.json` is `{"url": "https://x-access-token:ghp_xxx@github.com/delian/ddflow-mcp.git", "vcs_info": {...}}`, `direct_url()` returns that credential-bearing URL verbatim, and for any editable/local/archive install under a home directory it returns a `file:///home/...` URL that names the home directory un-normalised — directly contradicting the module's own documented guarantee. If the invariant is to hold, this accessor must not be part of the public surface (or must strip/normalise `url`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py: `direct_url`

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `.kind == "archive"` for a `direct_url.json` of `{"url": "https://example.invalid/a.tar.gz", "archive_info": {}}`. The change's stated contract enumerates the install kind as a closed set: `index|vcs|local-dir|editable|source-tree`. `archive` is not in that set. So a helper written to the described contract will map an `archive_info` direct_url onto one of the five documented kinds (e.g. `index`/`unknown`), and this assertion fails; conversely, if the helper does return `archive`, the documented kind enum in the change description is wrong. Concretely, with the fixture direct_url above, `installed(...).kind` is required by the test to be `"archive"`, which is outside the set of values the interface is declared to produce — the test and the contract cannot both be right.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_install_info.py:80-83 (`test_archive_install`)

chunk_findings.detail: The documented vocabulary for the public helper is `install kind (index|vcs|local-dir|editable|source-tree)` (and nothing else is enumerated), but the new tests pin two additional kinds that the contract never lists: `archive` here and `unknown` in `test_no_distribution_outside_a_checkout_is_unknown`. The change is therefore self-inconsistent, and the more consequential reading is that the helper mislabels the most common real install path: PEP 610 says `direct_url.json` *is* written for an sdist fetched from an index (pip records `{"url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/.../ddflow_mcp-1.0.tar.gz", "archive_info": {...}}`), so a plain `pip install ddflow-mcp` on a machine without a wheel gets `kind == "archive"` rather than the documented `index`. Any consumer (or the `ddflow --version` details in the intent) that treats `kind == "index"` as "installed normally from PyPI, no commit / not editable" will silently mis-handle sdist installs, and a caller that matches on the documented `Literal` has no case for `archive`/`unknown`. Either the test assertion at line 81 should be `"index"` (classifying archive_info whose URL is an index artifact as an index install) or the documented set must be extended to include `archive` and `unknown`; as written, one of the two is wrong.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_install_info.py:79-82 (`test_archive_install`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`install_info(root=...)` documents `root` as "the directory holding the `ddflow` package", and it uses `root` for every other decision (`own_distribution(root)`, `is_own_dev_tree(root)`, `_git(root, ...)`, `location`), but it computes `from_source` from `running_from_source()`, which only ever inspects `Path(__file__).resolve()` and never the `root` argument. As a result, the classification of any explicit `root` depends on where the *reviewing interpreter's* `ddflow` happens to live, not on `root`.

Concrete failure: take a fixture directory `/tmp/fix` that contains `ddflow_mcp-0.1.dist-info/direct_url.json` = `{"url": "https://github.com/delian/ddflow-mcp.git", "vcs_info": {"commit_id": "abc123", "requested_revision": "main"}}` (a "vcs" fixture, which may legitimately have no `ddflow/` package dir). Call `install_info(root=/tmp/fix)`.

- When the tests are run from the repo checkout (the normal case for this project's own tests, where `ddflow/services/install_info.py` is not under `site-packages`), `running_from_source()` returns `True`, so line ~182 discards the fixture's `direct_url.json` via `record = _editable_record(root)` (which finds nothing editable pointing at `/tmp/fix` and returns `None`). `_kind(dist, None, True)` then returns `"source-tree"` instead of `"vcs"`, and `commit` falls to `_git(root, "rev-parse", "HEAD")`, which is `None` because `/tmp/fix` is not a git repo — so the recorded `"abc123"` is lost too.
- When the same call is made by an interpreter whose `ddflow` is installed in `site-packages`, `running_from_source()` returns `False`, the `vcs_info` record is kept, and the call returns `kind="vcs", commit="abc123"`.

Same input, two different answers, decided by how the caller's own installation is laid out. `from_source` needs to be derived from `root` (e.g. `running_from_source(root)` testing `root` for `site-packages`/`dist-packages` parts) so that the `root` parameter is honoured consistently with `is_own_dev_tree(root)` and `location`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py: install_info(`from_source = running_from_source()`)

chunk_findings.detail: `install_info` does `dist = own_distribution(root)` and then `record = _direct_url(dist)`. `_direct_url` treats a `None` argument as "look up the default distribution" (`dist = dist if dist is not None else own_distribution()`), so when the caller-supplied `root` contains no dist-info the helper silently reads the *running* installation's `direct_url.json` instead of the tree it was asked about. Concrete case: `install_info(root=<fake site-packages dir containing ddflow/ but no dist-info>)` (the "unknown kind" fixture the change explicitly calls for) evaluated in an environment where ddflow-mcp is installed from a VCS URL. `dist` is `None`, `from_source` is `False` because the path contains `site-packages` (so the `_editable_record` override is not taken), and therefore `record` becomes the running install's `vcs_info` record — `kind` comes back `"vcs"` and `commit` is that install's commit, not `"unknown"` for the given root. The `None` sentinel in `_direct_url` conflates "no distribution" with "use the default", which only matters for the public `root` parameter but silently returns another install's identity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py `install_info` → `_direct_url`

chunk_findings.detail: The regex only enforces a *trailing* component boundary: `re.escape(home) + r"(?=/|$|[^\w.-])"`. There is no leading boundary, so a home string that occurs as the suffix of a longer path component is still replaced. With `home == "/home/ann"`, `normalise_path("/srv/backup/home/ann/ddflow")` matches `/home/ann` at index 11 and returns `/srv/backup~/ddflow` — a mangled path that no longer corresponds to any real directory, contradicting the in-code comment "Only at a path-component boundary". A leading lookbehind (`(?<![\w.-])`, i.e. require start-of-string or a separator before the home match) is needed to only replace whole components.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py `normalise_path`

chunk_findings.detail: `tomllib.loads(...).get("project", {}).get("name")` crashes when `project` parses but is not a table. A `pyproject.toml` containing `project = "x"` is valid TOML, so `tomllib.loads` succeeds, `.get("project", {})` returns the string `"x"`, and `.get("name")` raises `AttributeError`. The surrounding `except (OSError, ValueError)` does not catch it, so `install_info(root=...)` / `is_own_dev_tree(root)` propagates the exception instead of falling back to the remote-origin check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py `is_own_dev_tree`

chunk_findings.detail: An unreadable `direct_url.json` is reported as an index install, contradicting the module's own guarantee. `_direct_url` claims: "None when there is none (an index install, no distribution, **or an unreadable file** — the last is also 'not evidence of an index', and `kind` says so)." But `_direct_url` gets "unreadable" and "missing" from the same source: `Distribution.read_text` swallows `PermissionError`/`IsADirectoryError` and returns `None`, so an existing-but-unreadable file is indistinguishable from an absent file. `_kind(dist, record=None, from_source=False)` then returns `"index"` whenever `dist is not None`, and `installed_from_index()` also returns `True` (`dist.read_text("direct_url.json") is None`). Concrete input: `pip install git+https://github.com/delian/ddflow-mcp`, then `chmod 000` on the `direct_url.json` inside `ddflow_mcp-*.dist-info` (a normal user, not root, so `PermissionError` is raised and suppressed). `install_info()` now returns `kind="index", commit=None` for a VCS install, and `installed_from_index()` returns `True`, so `adopt` would conclude `uvx ddflow-mcp` reaches the same project when it does not. Note the inconsistency: a *corrupt* (readable but invalid) `direct_url.json` correctly yields `"unknown"`, while an unreadable one yields `"index"`; both are equally "not evidence of an index".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:_direct_url / _kind / installed_from_index

chunk_findings.detail: For a `local-dir` install the reported `location` is the running package's parent (site-packages), not the directory it was installed from. In `install_info`, `root` defaults to `_paths.package_parent()`, and a non-editable `pip install /some/dir` copies the code into site-packages (so `running_from_source(root)` is `False` and `root` is the site-packages directory). The record it reads has `dir_info.editable == false`, so `_kind` returns `"local-dir"`, and `location = normalise_path(root)` returns the site-packages path, e.g. `~/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages`, while the meaningful install directory (`/some/dir`) sits unused in the record's `url`. Input: `pip install /home/ann/code/ddflow` (non-editable) then `import ddflow; install_info()` → `location` names the venv's site-packages instead of `/home/ann/code/ddflow`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:install_info (location computation for `kind == "local-dir"`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change's own stated contract says the helper returns `install kind (index|vcs|local-dir|editable|source-tree)`, but this test asserts a seventh kind, `"archive"`, for a `direct_url.json` containing `archive_info` (`installed({"url": "https://example.invalid/a.tar.gz", "archive_info": {}}).kind == "archive"`), and `test_no_distribution_outside_a_checkout_is_unknown` adds `"unknown"` as well. The concrete consumer failure: a wheel installed from an index records exactly this shape of PEP 610 data (pip writes `direct_url.json` with `archive_info` for downloads it can URL-address), so `install_info()` reports `kind == "archive"` for what the change documents as an `index` install, and the documented `index` branch (tested with `direct_url=None`) is only reached when no `direct_url.json` exists at all. A caller (the upstream report this phase is for) that switches on the documented five-kind set will have an unhandled case for the most common real installation. Either the documented enum has to include `archive`/`unknown` or the classifier/tests must fold those inputs into the documented kinds; as written the public contract and the asserted behaviour disagree.

chunk_findings.detail: `installed_from_index()` decides solely on `own_distribution()` + `_direct_url()`, with no `running_from_source()` guard. `own_distribution()` looks in the directory holding the package (`_paths.package_parent()`), which for a source checkout is the repo root. A checkout that has been built or editable-installed leaves a `ddflow_mcp.egg-info` directory in that root (setuptools/`pip install -e .`/`python -m build` all write it). importlib.metadata yields that egg-info for `name="ddflow-mcp"`, `egg-info` dirs never contain `direct_url.json`, so `_direct_url()` returns `None` and `installed_from_index()` returns `True`. Concretely: `pip install -e .` then run `ddflow` from the checkout → `installed_from_index()` reports `True`, i.e. "came from the index, `uvx ddflow-mcp` reaches the same project", which is exactly the state the module's own comment in `install_info` forbids ("A checkout is never an index install, even when a build leaves an egg-info (no direct_url.json) beside it"). The consequence is that a caller (adopt/enforce) that uses this to pick the index/`uvx` launch path would run the published package instead of the running dev checkout. `install_info()` avoids this by overwriting `record` with `_editable_record()` when `from_source`, but the public `installed_from_index()` does not, so it contradicts the documented invariant for any checkout carrying an egg-info.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py :: `installed_from_index`

chunk_findings.detail:
The `from_source` heuristic equates "the package does not live under a `site-packages`/`dist-packages` directory" with "this is a checkout," and `install_info` then **discards the real PEP 610 record** whenever `from_source` is true:

```python
if from_source:
    record = _editable_record(root)   # None for any non-editable install outside site-packages
```

Concrete failure: `pip install --target=/opt/x ddflow-mcp` (from the index). The dist-info lands directly in `/opt/x`, so `_paths.package_parent()` is `/opt/x`, which contains no `site-packages` part, so `running_from_source(/opt/x)` returns `True`. There is no `direct_url.json` (index install), and `_editable_record(/opt/x)` returns `None`, so `_kind(None, None, True)` returns `"source-tree"`. `install_info()` therefore reports `kind="source-tree"` and a `location` of `/opt/x` for what is actually an index install (its own docstring/comment says "A checkout is never an index install"). The same happens for a `pip install` from a local directory into a `--target`/`--prefix` tree: the `dir_info` record is thrown away and a `local-dir` install is reported as `source-tree`. `installed_from_index()`, which is derived from the same metadata, still returns `True` here, so the two public helpers disagree about the same installation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py `install_info` / `running_from_source`

chunk_findings.detail: `installed_from_index()` returns `True` whenever `own_distribution()` finds a distribution whose `direct_url.json` is missing, without ever consulting `running_from_source()`. For a source checkout that carries an `*.egg-info` beside the package (exactly the case the new code comments on: "even when a build leaves an egg-info (no direct_url.json) beside it"), `own_distribution()` finds that egg-info, `_direct_url()` returns `None`, and `installed_from_index()` returns `True`. But `install_info()` reports `kind="source-tree"` for the same tree, i.e. the helper claims `uvx ddflow-mcp` reaches "the same project" while the running code is a dev checkout, not the index build.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py `installed_from_index`

chunk_findings.detail: `_kind` guards the top-level shape of the record and guards `vcs_info` with `isinstance(..., dict)`, but it does not guard the nested `dir_info` value, and `_editable_record` has the same gap. Given a parseable `direct_url.json` whose `dir_info` is present but not a mapping (e.g. `{"url": "file:///x", "dir_info": "bogus"}`), `_direct_url` returns the dict (top-level `isinstance(record, dict)` passes), then `_kind` evaluates `(record["dir_info"] or {}).get("editable")`; because `"bogus"` is truthy, `or {}` does not substitute, so `"bogus".get(...)` raises `AttributeError`. This propagates out of the public `install_info()` (and out of `_editable_record` on the same input), so instead of degrading to `kind="unknown"`/`local-dir` as the module does for a missing or unreadable file, the helper crashes. Fix is to coerce `dir_info` with `isinstance(..., dict)` (mirroring the `vcs_info` check) in both places.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:139 (`_kind`) and :96 (`_editable_record`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_direct_url` calls `dist.read_text("direct_url.json")` outside any try, and `importlib.metadata.Distribution.read_text` only suppresses `FileNotFoundError, IsADirectoryError, KeyError, NotADirectoryError, PermissionError`. A `direct_url.json` that exists but is not valid UTF-8 (e.g. contains the bytes `b"\xff\xfe"`, as can happen with a partially written/corrupted file) makes `Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` raise `UnicodeDecodeError`, which is a `ValueError` but is raised before the `try/except ValueError` around `json.loads`. The exception therefore propagates out of `install_info()` and `installed_from_index()` instead of the intended `{}` ("present but unreadable"), contradicting the comment two lines below. Concrete: a dist-info directory containing `direct_url.json` = `b"\xff"` makes `install_info()` crash rather than return `kind == "unknown"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:_direct_url

chunk_findings.detail: `_version` only falls back to `import ddflow` when `dist.version` *raises*, but `importlib.metadata.Distribution.version` is `self.metadata['Version']`, and `email.message.Message.__getitem__` returns `None` for a missing header (it does not raise). So a dist-info whose `METADATA` has no `Version:` field makes `dist.version` return `None`; `_version` returns that `None` (no exception is raised), so `InstallInfo.version` is `None` even though the field is annotated `str` and the `import ddflow` fallback exists exactly for the case where the distribution provides no usable version.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:_version

chunk_findings.detail:
The stated public contract for this helper is `install kind (index|vcs|local-dir|editable|source-tree)` — exactly five values. `test_archive_install` asserts a sixth value, `"archive"`, for `direct_url.json = {"url": "https://example.invalid/a.tar.gz", "archive_info": {}}`:

```python
def test_archive_install(installed):
    assert installed({"url": "https://example.invalid/a.tar.gz", "archive_info": {}}).kind == "archive"
```

So the helper returns `kind == "archive"` for any PEP 610 archive-URL install (e.g. `pip install https://.../ddflow_mcp.tar.gz`). Any caller that dispatches on the documented five-kind set — the `ddflow --version` plumbing and the upstream-reporting consumer this change exists to feed — hits its fall-through path for such an install and reports the wrong install kind (or drops it). If `archive` is intended, it has to be part of the contract and handled by those consumers; otherwise an `archive_info` record should be mapped onto one of the five documented kinds. (Note this contradicts the change's own enumerated kind list, which contains no `archive`.)
chunk_findings.title: `tests/test_install_info.py::test_archive_install`

chunk_findings.detail: `normalise_traceback` only recognises ddflow frame paths that contain the literal substring `/ddflow/` with a leading slash. A relative path like `File "ddflow/cli.py", line 10, in main` — which is what CPython emits for the entry script when the tool is run from its own repo as `python ddflow/cli.py`, i.e. the own-dev-tree case the acceptance calls out — is treated as operator code. `_frame_path` falls through to the final branch and returns `("<path>/cli.py", False)`, so the frame becomes `File "<path>/cli.py"` and `drop_source=True` discards the following source line. Concretely, `normalise_traceback('  File "ddflow/cli.py", line 10, in main\n    raise SystemExit(1)')` returns `'  File "<path>/cli.py", line 10, in main'`, dropping the public ddflow source line. This contradicts the module docstring (“A frame inside ddflow becomes `ddflow/<module path>` (its source line is public code and stays)”) and the acceptance requirement “normalised ddflow/ frames”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bugreport.py:normalise_traceback / _frame_path

chunk_findings.detail: When `subcommands` is not supplied — which is the default on the `Failure` dataclass — `redact_argv` keeps any leading run of lowercase words, not just the CLI’s own verbs. A positional value that happens to match `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,23}` is therefore rendered verbatim, e.g. `redact_argv(["ddflow", "report", "my-secret-project"])` returns `["ddflow", "report", "my-secret-project"]`, leaking the project slug instead of `<arg>`; expected `["ddflow", "report", "<arg>"]`. Similarly, because any token starting with `-` is unconditionally treated as a flag name, a value such as `--token -hunter2` is returned unchanged (`["ddflow", "--token", "-hunter2"]`) rather than `--token <value>`. This violates the stated guarantee that argv is sent with “every value removed” / “command argv with values redacted”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bugreport.py:redact_argv

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_value_of_previous` only recognises an argument as "the value of the preceding flag" when the preceding token is a *long* flag (`out[-1].startswith("--")`) and the token is longer than `_SHORT_FLAG` chars. A value that itself begins with `-` after a short flag (or after a long flag but with a short token) therefore falls into the flag branch and is emitted verbatim as if it were a flag name, not replaced by `<value>`. Concretely, `redact_argv(["ddflow", "login", "-p", "-hunter2"], ("login",))` returns `["ddflow", "login", "-p", "-hunter2"]` — the `-p` value `-hunter2` survives unredacted, contradicting the module docstring ("every flag name, and `<value>` / `<arg>` in place of anything else") and the stated acceptance that argv carries values redacted. The same path leaks a double-dash value (`redact_argv(["ddflow", "--password", "--secret"])` yields `"--secret"`), and the length test is inconsistent: `["ddflow", "--limit", "-1"]` emits `-1` as a flag while `["ddflow", "--limit", "-10"]` correctly emits `<value>`, so the classification is wrong for a plain negative argument too. Any token a caller passes as an argument value that happens to start with `-` is exposed.
chunk_findings.title: `redact_argv` / `_is_value_of_previous` (ddflow/services/bugreport.py)

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_value_of_previous` only recognises a token as a flag's value when the token begins with a *single* dash (`not tok.startswith("--")` in the guard). Any value that itself begins with `--` therefore falls into the flag branch and is appended to the argv verbatim, so the bundle ships a secret that the module exists to remove. `redact_argv(["ddflow", "report", "--token", "--s3cr3t"])` returns `["ddflow", "report", "--token", "--s3cr3t"]` (not `... "--token", "<value>"`), and that literal is what ends up in `command.argv` in both the markdown `## Command` block and the canonical JSON – the caller's CLI parses `--s3cr3t` as the value of `--token`, not as a flag name. The same hole exists for dash values after a short flag, e.g. `redact_argv(["ddflow", "report", "-t", "-s3cr3t"])` → `["ddflow", "report", "-t", "-s3cr3t"]`, because the helper requires `out[-1].startswith("--")`. Any credential/password that happens to start with `-` is thus reported unredacted, which breaks "command argv with values redacted".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bugreport.py:redact_argv (via `_is_value_of_previous`)

chunk_findings.detail: Only the environment *values* pass through `clean`/`redact_report`; the keys are copied into the bundle untouched, so they bypass the redaction, the surrogate scrub and the `KNOB_ALLOWLIST` filtering that the module docstring promises for "every string that is left". Given `env={"/home/alice/project": "1"}`, `data["environment"]` (and therefore the markdown `- /home/alice/project: 1` line and the canonical JSON digested by `digest_of`) contains the literal home-repo path even though `scrub.home`/`scrub.repo_root` are set and the same string as a *value* would be scrubbed. The same applies to a lone-surrogate key, which would make `digest_of`'s `body.encode("utf-8")` raise instead of being replaced by `_SURROGATES`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bugreport.py:build_bundle (`"environment": {k: clean(v) ...}`)

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert seen == [out.data["title"]] or seen == [f"claim crashes in {PROJECT}"]` explicitly accepts the pre-redaction title being handed to the dedupe provider. With the default scrub (`names=[PROJECT]`, `home=HOME`) a correct bundle must invoke the provider with the redacted title (e.g. `claim crashes in <project>`); the second disjunct lets a regression pass in which `build_bundle` forwards the raw title (`claim crashes in secretproj`, or a real title containing a home path/IP/email) into `B.local_candidates`. That query is outside the sanitized bundle and can be logged/persisted, so the test cannot detect the very leak the redaction is meant to prevent—making the dedupe path a silent escape hatch for private title text.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bugreport_bundle.py::test_candidates_use_the_title_and_unavailable_is_said

chunk_findings.detail:
`redact_argv` treats any single-dash token that matches `_FLAG` (`--?[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,40}`) as a *flag name* and emits it verbatim, so a short flag with an attached value leaks that value. `Failure.flags` defaults to `None` and `redact_argv` defaults `flags=None`, in which case `ok = bool(_FLAG.fullmatch(name))` — and `-psecret`, `-I/home/x`, `-ofile.o`, etc. all fullmatch, so the whole token is appended unchanged:

```
redact_argv(["ddflow","run","-psecret"], subcommands=["run"])  # flags=None (default)
-> ["ddflow", "run", "-psecret"]      # "secret" survives
```

`clean` (redact_report) only knows hostname/names/home/repo_root/cfg, so an opaque value like `-psecret` is not removed downstream. This directly contradicts the module's stated guarantee that "a dash-led secret ... never survives as one" and the intent sentence "command argv with values redacted": the two examples the docstring worries about (`--token -hunter2`, `-p --s3cr3t`) are *separate* tokens and are handled, but the ubiquitous attached-value form `-psecret` is not. The bug only closes when the caller remembers to pass `flags` (then `name in known` is False and it becomes `<flag>`), i.e. the sanitizer's safety depends on an optional argument whose default is unsafe. A token such as `--passwordhunter2` (long flag, value attached without `=`) leaks the same way.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bugreport.py:redact_argv

chunk_findings.detail: The test’s pass depends on the mutable contents of the developer’s `.ddflow/events` log, not on the code under test. Given a checkout whose log contains `bug.found` events but whose logged `data.summary` strings happen to be clean (for example `"list index out of range"` with no path, IP address, e-mail, hostname or project name), every `_build(...)` call produces `out.redactions == {}`, so `dirty` remains 0 and the final `assert dirty, "real bug texts carry private text; something must have been redacted"` fails even though the generated bundle is correctly sanitised. The test should either assert a property of the bundle for each summary or skip when no summary triggers redaction.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bugreport_bundle.py:test_bundles_from_real_bug_texts_in_the_logs_leak_nothing (final `assert dirty`)

chunk_findings.detail: The “odd” failure puts the private project name inside `error_class` (`error_class="x y\nz" + PROJECT`). The assertion checks only `odd.markdown`, so a leak of the same value through the other half of the bundle (`odd.json` / `odd.rendered`) is not detected. Since the acceptance criterion is that the whole bundle is sanitised, this test can pass while `out.json` still contains the raw project name. The check should be `assert PROJECT not in odd.markdown + odd.json`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bugreport_bundle.py:test_exit_code_and_class_recorded (`assert PROJECT not in odd.markdown`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`redact_argv` decides a token is a flag's value only when the *rendered* previous output token literally starts with `-` and has no `=`. When the preceding flag was itself rendered as the placeholder `<flag>` (which happens whenever `flags` is `None` and the flag text doesn't match `_FLAG`, or whenever `flags` is given and the flag is not among the known names), or when the value is attached to a getopt-style short option, that guard is false, so a dash-led value falls into the "treat as a flag name" branch and, with `known is None`, is emitted verbatim because `_FLAG.fullmatch` says it "looks like a flag". This contradicts the module's stated guarantee that dash-led secrets "never survive as one".

Concrete inputs (both with the documented defaults `subcommands=None, flags=None`):

- `redact_argv(["ddflow", "-psecret"])` returns `["ddflow", "-psecret"]` instead of `["ddflow", "<flag>", "<value>"]` (or at least `["ddflow", "<flag>"]`). `-psecret` is the getopt-concatenated form of `-p secret`, so the secret is emitted verbatim. This is the same class of input the docstring claims to handle (`-p --s3cr3t`), only attached instead of separate.
- `redact_argv(["ddflow", "--cfg.x", "-hunter2"])` returns `["ddflow", "<flag>", "-hunter2"]`: `--cfg.x` fails `_FLAG.fullmatch` (the `.` is disallowed) and is shown as `<flag>`, so the following `-hunter2` is no longer recognized as a value and is passed through verbatim.

In both cases the value is leaked into the bundle (`command.argv` is `[clean(t) for t in redact_argv(...)]`, so the only protection left is `redact_report`, which redacts the machine/project names it was given, not arbitrary credentials embedded in argv). The trigger for the first case is the default `flags=None`; note `Failure.flags` also defaults to `None`, so a caller that constructs `Failure` without populating flags takes this path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bugreport.py :: redact_argv (flag/value branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The leak check for the operator's raw name is written as `assert "someone" not in out.markdown.replace("someone-", "")`. By stripping every occurrence of `someone-` from the *markdown* before the membership test, the assertion can no longer observe exactly the shape of leak it is meant to guard against: a rendering of the raw operator identity followed by a hyphen. With the fixture input `on_behalf_of_operator="someone"` (the value used in both `_build()` and the `named = _build(...)` call in the same test), if the bundle rendered the operator in the markdown as e.g. `someone-1` (a name-derived alias, an alias-map entry such as `someone-4f2a → op-1`, or any `someone-<suffix>` token) the expression under test becomes `"someone" not in "<...>1<...>"`, which passes — even though the raw operator name is present in the artifact. Only the JSON alias is actually verified (`prov["on_behalf_of_operator"] == "op-1"`); the markdown, which is what a human reads and what the acceptance criterion cares about, is effectively unchecked for this value. The assertion should be evaluated against the unmodified markdown (no substring replacement), and the `replace()` call removed so that any `someone`-prefixed token fails the test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bugreport_bundle.py:test_provenance_aliases_and_detector

chunk_findings.detail: With the documented default `flags=None` (the signature's default, and the `Failure.flags` default), the fallback classifier `bool(_FLAG.fullmatch(name))` treats the *whole* dash-led token as a flag name whenever it matches `--?[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,40}`. A short option with an attached value therefore survives verbatim. Concrete input: `redact_argv(["ddflow", "-psecret"])` returns `["ddflow", "-psecret"]` — the value `secret` is emitted unredacted, contradicting the module contract that "argv with every value removed" and the docstring's promise that a dash-led secret "never survives as one". (When `flags` *is* supplied as `["-p"]`, the same call correctly yields `["ddflow", "<flag>"]`, so the leak is specific to the default path; the same holds for a standalone `-hunter2` in flag position.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bugreport.py:redact_argv

chunk_findings.detail: When a value is truncated, the text is passed through the counting wrapper `clean` twice: once on the full `value` and again on `text[: limit - len(_CUT)]`. Redactions in the retained prefix are counted twice, and redactions in the portion that is truncated away are counted even though they never appear in the bundle. Input example: `title = "contact a@b.com " + "x"*200` (length > `TITLE_MAX`) increments the redaction count for that kind twice even though the rendered title contains the pattern only once, so `data["redactions"]` (and `Bundle.redactions`) no longer reflects what is actually in the bundle.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/bugreport.py:build_bundle (`bounded`)

chunk_findings.detail: The final `assert dirty` is not a property of the bundle builder but of the current checkout's mutable `.ddflow/events` log. It only passes if at least one real `bug.found` event produces a nonzero redaction count, because `dirty` is incremented solely from `sum(out.redactions.values()) > 0`. The `pytest.skip` fires only when there are zero `bug.found` events. Given a log that contains a `bug.found` event with an already-generic summary and event subject (e.g. summary "command failed", subject "T-1"), `bugs` is non-empty, the skip is bypassed, every bundle built in the loop has empty `redactions`, `dirty` remains 0, and the test fails even though nothing leaked. The `host = max(counts, key=counts.__getitem__)` line has the same log-content dependence in the opposite direction: if the log's `bug.found` events all have empty/missing `agent` fields, `counts` is empty and `max()` raises `ValueError` instead of skipping.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bugreport_bundle.py::test_bundles_from_real_bug_texts_in_the_logs_leak_nothing
